# watchpoint_tenant_monitoring_policy (Resource)

Tenant-wide monitor change policy: lock Terraform-managed monitors against edits made outside Terraform, and require approval for monitor changes in chosen environments. One per tenant. The lock needs the Terraform managed lock feature and the approval settings need the change approvals feature; only the attributes you set are sent, so a tenant with one feature can still manage it. While approvals are on for an environment, Terraform writes to its monitors fail with `approval_required` like any other caller. Destroying the resource turns the lock and approvals off. Requires `settings.manage`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "watchpoint_tenant_monitoring_policy" "this" {
  lock_terraform_managed   = true
  approval_environment_ids = [watchpoint_environment.production.id]
  approval_min_approvers   = 2
  approval_allow_self      = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `approval_allow_self` (Boolean) Whether the requester may approve their own change.
- `approval_environment_ids` (Set of String) Environments (`watchpoint_environment` ids) whose monitor changes need approval. An empty set turns approvals off.
- `approval_min_approvers` (Number) Approvals a change needs, 1 to 5.
- `lock_terraform_managed` (Boolean) Refuse edits, deletes and reverts of Terraform-managed monitors made outside Terraform.

### Read-Only

- `approvals_available` (Boolean) Whether the tenant's plan includes change approvals.
- `id` (String) The tenant ID.
- `lock_available` (Boolean) Whether the tenant's plan includes the Terraform managed lock.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import watchpoint_tenant_monitoring_policy.this <tenant-id>
```
